newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real dips 0.01 pct on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real dips 0.01 pct on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real dipped 0.01 percent on net dollar inflows to close at 1.0724 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank depreciated the mini-band by 0.09 percent to between 1.0720 and 1.0770 reais per dollar.

The previous mini-band was set on Thursday at between 1.0710 and 1.0760 per greenback. So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.19 percent against the dollar compared to an average monthly drop of between 0.57 and 0.63 percent in the past half year.

Analysts said the real dropped less than the decline in the mini-band mostly due to dollar inflows. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts at 1640 local/1940 GMT showed a $220 million surplus.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.05 percent to end at 1.0771 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real closed flat at 1.130 per dollar, traders said.
